You are designing and prototyping multiplayer for a browser Minecraft 26.2 recreation, connecting to a local Paper 26.2 server. Project: C:\Users\zht\Documents\Qoder\2026-11-01\4194ac07\webcraft26. The user explicitly allows a Paper plugin and expects browser clients to join a real Paper 26.2 world (plugins may run). Browsers cannot open raw TCP/Java protocol sockets, and full Java login/encryption is out of scope for this first milestone.

CRITICAL SAFETY / OWNERSHIP:
- You own ONLY a new directory bridge/ (and may add a short doc there). Do NOT edit src/, index.html, package.json, public/mc or any game files. Do not modify, start, stop, or copy the user's live server at G:/Minecraftserver/DaemonData/Servers/1. Do not install system-wide packages. Do not deploy anything. Do not download unofficial prebuilt jars/binaries. Do not run heavy Gradle/Maven builds that exceed a few minutes without reporting; prefer writing buildable source + exact commands.
- Existing official Paper jars (paper-26.2.jar and builds 60/107/112/119/129) are at G:/Minecraftserver/DaemonData/Servers/1. A Java runtime may be provided by MSLX or bundled elsewhere; `java` is not on the bash PATH. Search read-only (e.g. common MSLX dirs, G: drive) to locate one, but do not modify it.

Goal: deliver the most practical, working foundation for browser ↔ Paper 26.2 multiplayer:
1. Inspect the local Paper 26.2 jar manifests/API version read-only, and determine if a plugin can embed a WebSocket/HTTP server with Paper-provided dependencies or a shaded Jetty/Netty. Prefer a Paper plugin that hosts a WebSocket endpoint, because using Bukkit/Paper world APIs is far more robust than reimplementing the Java client protocol.
2. Design a server-authoritative bridge protocol for browser clients: hello/auth, join world, chunk section/block snapshot stream, block updates, player avatar spawn/move/look, entity position snapshots, chat, inventory handshake, ping. Use binary or compact JSON over WebSocket; document message schemas and rate limits briefly.
3. Implement a minimal buildable Paper plugin skeleton in bridge/paper-plugin/ (paper-plugin.yml/plugin.yml, build.gradle.kts or pom.xml, Java source) that:
   - starts a WebSocket endpoint on a configurable loopback port,
   - handles hello/join/leave, streams nearby blocks and periodic entity/player snapshots for a browser avatar (a server-side NPC representation; choose a display entity/armor stand or similar Paper API approach that other Java players can see, without NMS hacks if possible),
   - accepts block place/break intents validated against reach distance and applies them via Paper API,
   - broadcasts chat.
   It does not need full inventory/crafting yet, but the design must leave room for them. Avoid fake/incomplete code that cannot compile; keep the first vertical slice small.
4. If Java toolchain cannot be found, still deliver source + build config + protocol doc + exact validation steps, and clearly report the blocker. Do not claim it builds/runs unless verified.
5. Provide a tiny standalone Node WebSocket test client under bridge/test-client/ (no new npm deps if possible; use ws if already available or document install), and an install/run README explaining offline-mode/online-mode, firewall, and that the live server is untouched. The browser frontend integration will be done later by the main agent; expose a clean protocol.
6. Do NOT begin implementing the vanilla Java client protocol or Mineflayer. The plugin sidecar architecture is the chosen approach. If you believe a different architecture is clearly superior, explain in <150 words but still deliver the plugin skeleton.

Report (<500 words): what you inspected, chosen architecture and why, exact files, build/run status and blockers, protocol summary, and what the main agent must do next to wire the browser. Be explicit about anything unverified.

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Build WebCraftBridge with the JDK 25 bundled with MSLX, without Gradle or network access.

.DESCRIPTION
  Extracts the official paper-api jar that is already bundled inside a Paper 26.2 jar
  (read-only) into %TEMP%, compiles src/main/java with javac --release 25, and packages
  plugin.yml + config.yml into build/dist/WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar.

  Nothing under G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Servers\1 is modified. The server does not
  need to be stopped. This only reads the Paper jar.

.EXAMPLE
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build-local.ps1
#>
param(
    [string]$PaperJar = "G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Servers\1\paper-26.2-129.jar",
    [string]$JdkHome = "G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Tools\Java\25",
    # Optional: point at a paper-api jar you already have. If empty, it is extracted from PaperJar.
    [string]$ApiJar = "",
    [string]$OutputDirectory = ""
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$root = $PSScriptRoot
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($OutputDirectory)) {
    $OutputDirectory = Join-Path $root "build"
}
$classes = Join-Path $OutputDirectory "classes"
$dist = Join-Path $OutputDirectory "dist"
$javac = Join-Path $JdkHome "bin\javac.exe"
$jarTool = Join-Path $JdkHome "bin\jar.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $javac)) {
    throw "javac not found at $javac. Pass -JdkHome <jdk-25-home>."
}
if (-not (Test-Path $jarTool)) {
    throw "jar tool not found at $jarTool."
}

$temporaryApi = $null
try {
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($ApiJar)) {
        if (-not (Test-Path $PaperJar)) {
            throw "Paper jar not found at $PaperJar. Pass -PaperJar <paper-26.2.jar>."
        }
        Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
        $zip = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead((Resolve-Path $PaperJar).Path)
        try {
            $entry = $zip.Entries |
                Where-Object { $_.FullName -match '^META-INF/libraries/io/papermc/paper/paper-api/.+/paper-api-.+\.jar$' } |
                Select-Object -First 1
            if ($null -eq $entry) {
                throw "No bundled paper-api jar found inside $PaperJar. Pass -ApiJar <paper-api.jar>."
            }
            $temporaryApi = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("webcraft-paper-api-" + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".jar")
            [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::ExtractToFile($entry, $temporaryApi, $true)
            $ApiJar = $temporaryApi
            Write-Host "Using bundled API: $($entry.FullName)"
        }
        finally {
            $zip.Dispose()
        }
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path $ApiJar)) {
        throw "paper-api jar not found at $ApiJar."
    }

    if (Test-Path $classes) {
        Remove-Item -Path $classes -Recurse -Force
    }
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $classes -Force | Out-Null
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dist -Force | Out-Null

    $sources = @(Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $root "src\main\java") -Recurse -Filter "*.java" |
        ForEach-Object { $_.FullName })
    if ($sources.Count -eq 0) {
        throw "No Java sources found under src/main/java."
    }

    Write-Host "Compiling $($sources.Count) source file(s) with $javac ..."
    & $javac "-encoding" "UTF-8" "--release" "25" "-Xlint:all" "-cp" $ApiJar "-d" $classes $sources
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "javac failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE."
    }

    Copy-Item -Path (Join-Path $root "src\main\resources\*") -Destination $classes -Recurse -Force

    $outputJar = Join-Path $dist "WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar"
    if (Test-Path $outputJar) {
        Remove-Item -Path $outputJar -Force
    }
    & $jarTool "--create" "--file" $outputJar "-C" $classes "."
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "jar failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE."
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Built: $outputJar"
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Install (only when you choose to restart your server):"
    Write-Host "  Copy-Item '$outputJar' 'G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Servers\1\plugins\'"
}
finally {
    if ($null -ne $temporaryApi -and (Test-Path $temporaryApi)) {
        Remove-Item -Path $temporaryApi -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

input.content:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Build WebCraftBridge with the JDK 25 bundled with MSLX, without Gradle or network access.

.DESCRIPTION
  Extracts the official paper-api jar that is already bundled inside a Paper 26.2 jar
  (read-only) into %TEMP%, adds the Paper runtime's compile-time libraries from the adjacent
  libraries/ directory, compiles src/main/java with javac --release 25, and packages
  plugin.yml + config.yml into build/dist/WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar.

  Nothing under G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Servers\1 is modified. The server does not
  need to be stopped. This only reads Paper jars/library files.

.EXAMPLE
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build-local.ps1

.EXAMPLE
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build-local.ps1 `
    -PaperJar "C:\paper\paper-26.2-129.jar" -JdkHome "C:\Java\jdk-25"
#>
param(
    [string]$PaperJar = "G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Servers\1\paper-26.2-129.jar",
    [string]$JdkHome = "G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Tools\Java\25",
    # Optional: point at a paper-api jar you already have. If empty, it is extracted from PaperJar.
    [string]$ApiJar = "",
    # Directory containing the Paper server's libraries/ folder. Defaults to the folder next to PaperJar.
    [string]$LibrariesDirectory = "",
    [string]$OutputDirectory = ""
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$root = $PSScriptRoot
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($OutputDirectory)) {
    $OutputDirectory = Join-Path $root "build"
}
$classes = Join-Path $OutputDirectory "classes"
$dist = Join-Path $OutputDirectory "dist"
$javac = Join-Path $JdkHome "bin\javac.exe"
$jarTool = Join-Path $JdkHome "bin\jar.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $javac)) {
    throw "javac not found at $javac. Pass -JdkHome <jdk-25-home>."
}
if (-not (Test-Path $jarTool)) {
    throw "jar tool not found at $jarTool."
}
if (-not (Test-Path $PaperJar)) {
    throw "Paper jar not found at $PaperJar. Pass -PaperJar <paper-26.2.jar>."
}
$paperPath = (Resolve-Path $PaperJar).Path
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($LibrariesDirectory)) {
    $LibrariesDirectory = Join-Path (Split-Path $paperPath) "libraries"
}
if (-not (Test-Path $LibrariesDirectory)) {
    throw "Paper libraries directory not found at $LibrariesDirectory. Pass -LibrariesDirectory."
}

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$classpath = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
$temporaryApi = $null
$temporaryBungee = $null

function Add-LibraryJar {
    param(
        [string]$RelativeDirectory,
        [string]$Filter
    )
    $directory = Join-Path $LibrariesDirectory $RelativeDirectory
    if (-not (Test-Path $directory)) {
        throw "Missing library directory: $directory"
    }
    $jar = Get-ChildItem -Path $directory -Recurse -Filter $Filter |
        Sort-Object FullName -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1
    if ($null -eq $jar) {
        throw "Missing $Filter under $directory"
    }
    $script:classpath.Add($jar.FullName)
}

try {
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($ApiJar)) {
        $zip = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead($paperPath)
        try {
            $entry = $zip.Entries |
                Where-Object { $_.FullName -match '^META-INF/libraries/io/papermc/paper/paper-api/.+/paper-api-.+\.jar$' } |
                Select-Object -First 1
            if ($null -eq $entry) {
                throw "No bundled paper-api jar found inside $PaperJar. Pass -ApiJar <paper-api.jar>."
            }
            $temporaryApi = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("webcraft-paper-api-" + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".jar")
            [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::ExtractToFile($entry, $temporaryApi, $true)
            $ApiJar = $temporaryApi
            Write-Host "Using bundled API: $($entry.FullName)"
        }
        finally {
            $zip.Dispose()
        }
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path $ApiJar)) {
        throw "paper-api jar not found at $ApiJar."
    }
    $classpath.Add((Resolve-Path $ApiJar).Path)

    # Compile-time dependencies declared by paper-api's POM. At runtime Paper supplies them.
    Add-LibraryJar "net\kyori\adventure-key" "adventure-key-*.jar"
    Add-LibraryJar "net\kyori\adventure-api" "adventure-api-*.jar"
    Add-LibraryJar "net\kyori\examination-api" "examination-api-*.jar"
    Add-LibraryJar "org\jetbrains\annotations" "annotations-*.jar"
    Add-LibraryJar "com\google\guava\guava" "guava-*.jar"

    # bungeecord-chat is needed because CommandSender.sendMessage is overloaded with BaseComponent.
    $bungeeDirectory = Join-Path $LibrariesDirectory "net\md-5\bungeecord-chat"
    if (Test-Path $bungeeDirectory) {
        Add-LibraryJar "net\md-5\bungeecord-chat" "bungeecord-chat-*.jar"
    }
    else {
        $zip = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead($paperPath)
        try {
            $bungeeEntry = $zip.Entries |
                Where-Object { $_.FullName -match '^META-INF/libraries/net/md-5/bungeecord-chat/.+\.jar$' } |
                Select-Object -First 1
            if ($null -eq $bungeeEntry) {
                throw "bungeecord-chat is missing from $LibrariesDirectory and $PaperJar."
            }
            $temporaryBungee = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("webcraft-bungee-chat-" + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".jar")
            [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::ExtractToFile($bungeeEntry, $temporaryBungee, $true)
            $classpath.Add($temporaryBungee)
        }
        finally {
            $zip.Dispose()
        }
    }

    if (Test-Path $classes) {
        Remove-Item -Path $classes -Recurse -Force
    }
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $classes -Force | Out-Null
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dist -Force | Out-Null

    $sources = @(Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $root "src\main\java") -Recurse -Filter "*.java" |
        ForEach-Object { $_.FullName })
    if ($sources.Count -eq 0) {
        throw "No Java sources found under src/main/java."
    }

    $compileClasspath = $classpath -join [System.IO.Path]::PathSeparator
    Write-Host "Compiling $($sources.Count) source file(s) with $javac ..."
    & $javac "-encoding" "UTF-8" "--release" "25" "-Xlint:deprecation" "-cp" $compileClasspath "-d" $classes $sources
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "javac failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE."
    }

    Copy-Item -Path (Join-Path $root "src\main\resources\*") -Destination $classes -Recurse -Force

    $outputJar = Join-Path $dist "WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar"
    if (Test-Path $outputJar) {
        Remove-Item -Path $outputJar -Force
    }
    & $jarTool "--create" "--file" $outputJar "-C" $classes "."
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "jar failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE."
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Built: $outputJar"
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Install (only when you choose to restart your server):"
    Write-Host "  Copy-Item '$outputJar' 'G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Servers\1\plugins\'"
}
finally {
    if ($null -ne $temporaryApi -and (Test-Path $temporaryApi)) {
        Remove-Item -Path $temporaryApi -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    if ($null -ne $temporaryBungee -and (Test-Path $temporaryBungee)) {
        Remove-Item -Path $temporaryBungee -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

# WebCraft 26.2 browser bridge

A Paper 26.2 plugin that hosts a loopback WebSocket endpoint. Browser clients join the real Paper
world through this sidecar instead of implementing the Java client protocol. The server remains
authoritative: block edits and avatar positions are validated and applied by the plugin using
Bukkit/Paper APIs, and Java players see each browser player as an armor-stand avatar.

This directory is intentionally self-contained. Nothing outside `bridge/` was modified.

## Status

- Plugin compiles against the exact Paper API bundled with the local Paper 26.2 build 129, and the
  jar packages successfully: `paper-plugin/build/dist/WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar`.
- The dependency-free WebSocket layer was tested outside Paper with Node 24: HTTP health, RFC 6455
  upgrade, masked text frames, a 120 KB server frame (64-bit length), echo and close.
- The plugin has **not** been loaded on Paper yet. The live server at
  `G:/Minecraftserver/DaemonData/Servers/1` was not installed into, started, stopped, reloaded or
  written to. World streaming, armor-stand visibility, block application and chat therefore remain
  to be validated on a server where a restart is allowed. See "Validation" below.

## Inspected facts (read-only)

- Live server process: `paper-26.2-129.jar`, port 25565, `online-mode=false`, whitelist off,
  `enforce-secure-profile=false`, management server disabled, RCON enabled.
- Paper `version.json`: Minecraft `26.2`, protocol `776`, Java `25`, world version `4903`.
- Bundled API: `io.papermc.paper:paper-api:26.2.build.129-stable` (exact artifact is published on
  Paper's Maven repository).
- Paper bundles Netty 4.2.15 under `libraries/`; Jetty is only a BOM, not a usable server. Plugin
  classloader access to server-internal libraries is not guaranteed, so this plugin uses **JDK-only
  sockets** and ships no shaded/copy dependencies. No third-party jars are downloaded.
- JDK 25 (Temurin 25.0.3) is at `G:/Minecraftserver/DaemonData/Tools/Java/25`; `javac` works.
- Gradle and Maven are not on PATH. A Gradle 9.1 distribution directory exists in the user profile,
  but the verified build path is `build-local.ps1` (javac + jar). `build.gradle.kts` is provided for a
  normal Gradle 9 / JDK 25 environment and is unverified here.

## Architecture

```
browser (Vite page, future)
   │  ws://127.0.0.1:8765/ws  (JSON, protocol v1)
   ▼
WebCraftBridge Paper plugin (this directory)
   │  hello / join / move / block intents / chat
   │  main-thread Bukkit calls
   ▼
Paper 26.2 world + Java players
   └─ armor-stand avatars visible to Java players (no NMS, no fake Player)
```

Why this and not the Java protocol: browsers cannot open raw TCP/Java sockets, and full login,
encryption and packet codecs would be a large, fragile reimplementation. A plugin already has
authoritative world access, block events, chat and entity APIs. A local WebSocket sidecar keeps the
browser integration to one clean JSON protocol. (If a future milestone needs Java players to see
browser players as real accounts, that is a separate vanilla-protocol proxy project.)

## Files

```
bridge/
  README.md
  PROTOCOL.md
  paper-plugin/
    plugin.yml                  legacy Bukkit descriptor (Paper still loads it; verified classes present)
    build.gradle.kts            alternative build, Gradle 9 + JDK 25 (not run here)
    settings.gradle.kts
    build-local.ps1             verified offline javac build using the local Paper API + libraries
    src/main/resources/config.yml
    src/main/java/io/webcraft/bridge/
      WebcraftBridgePlugin.java
      BridgeService.java        sessions, auth, join, movement, blocks, chat, snapshots
      BridgeSession.java
      BridgeConfig.java
      Avatar.java               invisible armor stand + equipment + name plate
      ChunkCodec.java           palette/RLE chunk sections
      Json.java                 dependency-free JSON
      RateLimiter.java
      ws/WsServer.java          raw ServerSocket + RFC 6455 handshake/framing
      ws/WsConnection.java
    src/test/java/.../WsSelfTest.java
  test-client/
    client.mjs                  dependency-free Node 22+ protocol client
    selftest.mjs                checks the WebSocket layer against WsSelfTest
```

## Build

Verified, offline, reads the local Paper jar read-only:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File bridge/paper-plugin/build-local.ps1
```

Output: `bridge/paper-plugin/build/dist/WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar`.

The script extracts the bundled `paper-api` and `bungeecord-chat` jars from Paper into `%TEMP%` and
adds Paper's existing `libraries/` compile dependencies (Adventure, annotations, Guava). It never
writes to the server directory. If you move the Paper jar, pass `-PaperJar`, `-JdkHome` and
`-LibrariesDirectory`.

Alternative (not verified here): install Gradle 9.x and JDK 25, set `JAVA_HOME`, then
`cd bridge/paper-plugin && gradle build`. The dependency coordinate
`io.papermc.paper:paper-api:26.2.build.129-stable` was confirmed to exist. The toolchain may try to
download a JDK; configure `org.gradle.java.installations.paths` if needed.

## Install and run (only when you choose to restart)

The live server is untouched. When a restart is acceptable:

1. Copy `WebCraftBridge-0.1.0.jar` to the server's `plugins/` directory.
2. Start the server normally. Do not use `/reload` for a plugin that owns sockets.
3. The log prints `WebSocket bridge listening on ws://127.0.0.1:8765/ws`.
4. Client config lives in `plugins/WebCraftBridge/config.yml`. `token` is empty by default
   (loopback only); `allowed-origins` defaults to the local Vite ports 5173/5174.
5. `/wcbridge status` shows the port, connected/joined counts and whether a token is required.
   `/wcbridge token` prints the configured token to an operator/console.

The plugin binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. No Windows firewall rule is needed for loopback. If you
change `bind-address` to a LAN address, set a long random `token`, add the exact page origin (for
example `http://192.168.1.20:5174`) and create a firewall rule for TCP 8765. There is no TLS (`wss`)
yet; prefer a reverse proxy or tunnel for anything non-loopback.

## Try the protocol

```bash
# Node 22+; no npm install needed (global WebSocket/fetch)
node bridge/test-client/client.mjs --name Alice
node bridge/test-client/client.mjs --url ws://127.0.0.1:8765/ws --name Bob --token dev-token
```

Commands: `/move x y z [yaw] [pitch]`, `/look yaw pitch`, `/place x y z minecraft:stone`,
`/break x y z`, `/chunk cx cz`, `/chat text` (or plain text), `/ping`, `/inv`, `/held 0`, `/quit`.
The client prints `joined`, chunk summaries, `players`, `entities`, block/chat events and errors.

Health check: `http://127.0.0.1:8765/health` returns JSON.

```powershell
# build first so build/classes exists
& "G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Tools\Java\25\bin\javac.exe" -encoding UTF-8 --release 25 `
  -cp build/classes -d build/selftest-classes src/test/java/io/webcraft/bridge/ws/WsSelfTest.java
& "G:\Minecraftserver\DaemonData\Tools\Java\25\bin\java.exe" -cp "build/classes;build/selftest-classes" `
  io.webcraft.bridge.ws.WsSelfTest
# in another shell, use the printed SELFTEST_PORT:
node bridge/test-client/selftest.mjs <port>
```

## Online-mode / offline-mode and identity

- Browser clients are **not** Minecraft accounts. They never authenticate with Mojang/Microsoft and
  are not covered by `whitelist.json`, bans, `online-mode` or `enforce-secure-profile`.
- The bridge works with either `online-mode=true` or `false`. The current server is offline-mode.
- Each browser gets a generated bridge session UUID and a visible armor-stand NPC named after it.
  Chat from the browser reaches Java players as `[Web] Name: text`; Java chat is forwarded to browser
  clients when the legacy `AsyncPlayerChatEvent` fires.
- Protect the bridge independently: loopback bind, Origin allowlist, and a token before exposing it.
  The token is a shared secret, not an account system.

## Validation and limits

Verified here: compilation, jar contents, YAML parsing, WebSocket upgrade/framing (including a
120 KB frame), health endpoint, Node client syntax. **Unverified:** Paper plugin loading, exact
`api-version` acceptance at runtime, chunk snapshot performance, armor-stand rendering and nameplate,
reach/block behavior, Java-block-event mirroring, legacy chat forwarding.

When a restart/test server is allowed, validate in this order:

1. Plugin enables without stack trace; log shows the bound port; `/wcbridge status` works.
2. `node client.mjs` receives `hello_ok`, `joined`, chunk sections, `stream_done`.
3. A Java player standing nearby sees the named armor stand; movement in the browser moves it.
4. Break/place a block from the client and from a Java player; both sides update.
5. Chat both directions; disconnect removes the armor stand.
6. Check `view-distance` cost on the main thread; lower it to 1 if needed.

Known limitations for this milestone: one configured world per session; no collision, gravity or
client physics (server clamps speed only); no inventory/crafting (empty virtual 41-slot handshake);
no skins or entity metadata; block physics/explosions are not streamed; chunk sections are JSON
(palette + RLE), not compressed binary; armor stands are not real players; no `wss`; no Java client
protocol and no Mineflayer.

Next for the browser agent: add a Vite WebSocket proxy (`/bridge` -> `ws://127.0.0.1:8765`, `ws: true`),
implement `hello`/`join`, render `section` palettes, apply `block` events, interpolate `player_move`
and `players`, and send rate-limited `move`/`look`/block intents. See `PROTOCOL.md`.

# WebCraft Bridge protocol v1

Transport: RFC 6455 WebSocket, **text frames only**, UTF-8 JSON. Default endpoint:
`ws://127.0.0.1:8765/ws` (configurable `port`/`path`). A `GET /health` endpoint returns JSON on the
same port. Protocol version: `1`.

The bridge is a sidecar to a Paper 26.2 server. Browser clients join one configured Bukkit world;
the server is authoritative for every block change and avatar position. There is no Java client
protocol, encryption or Mojang login.

## Authentication and origins

- `Origin` is checked against `allowed-origins` when the browser sends one. Non-browser clients may
  omit it only if `allow-missing-origin: true` (default, used by the Node test client).
- If `token` is configured, the client must supply it either as `?token=...` on the WebSocket URL or
  in the `hello` message. Both are accepted; the query form is convenient for browsers because they
  cannot set WebSocket headers.
- Empty token = no shared-secret check. Keep the bind address on loopback in that case.
- Max clients, hello timeout and rate limits are enforced per connection.

## Conventions

- Coordinates are Minecraft world coordinates in blocks: `+X` east, `+Y` up, `+Z` south. Positions
  are doubles; block coordinates are integers.
- `yaw` is degrees in `[-180, 180)`, `0` = south (+Z), `90` = west (-X), `180`/`-180` = north,
  `-90` = east. `pitch` is degrees in `[-90, 90]`, positive = down. The avatar's eye height is 1.62.
- Every message is a JSON object with `"t"` naming the type. Do not use `t` for payload data; ping
  uses `"id"`.
- Block states are Minecraft block-data strings, e.g. `"minecraft:stone"` or
  `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=north,half=bottom,shape=straight,waterlogged=false]"`. The server
  canonicalises them with `BlockData#getAsString()`. A browser renderer maps them to its own IDs.
- Player/entity IDs are UUID strings. A bridge player's ID is its session ID.
- `world` is the Bukkit world name; `dimension` is its namespaced key (e.g. `minecraft:overworld`).

## Session flow

```
client                                  plugin
  │  WS upgrade (Origin, optional ?token)  │
  │───────────────────────────────────────>│
  │  {"t":"hello","protocol":1,"name":...}  │
  │───────────────────────────────────────>│
  │  {"t":"hello_ok", ...}                  │
  │<───────────────────────────────────────│
  │  {"t":"join", optional x/y/z/yaw/pitch} │
  │───────────────────────────────────────>│
  │  {"t":"joined", ...} + {"t":"inv", ...} │
  │<───────────────────────────────────────│
  │  chunk_begin / section* / chunk_end ... │
  │<───────────────────────────────────────│
  │  {"t":"stream_done"}                    │
  │<───────────────────────────────────────│
  │  move / look / block_set / chat / ...   │
  │<───────────────────────────────────────│
  │  players / entities / block / chat ...  │
```

### Client → server

| `t` | Schema | Notes / limit |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | `{t, protocol:1, name, token?}` | Once. `name` matches `[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,16}`, unique among bridge sessions. Must arrive within 10 s of the upgrade. |
| `join` | `{t, x?, y?, z?, yaw?, pitch?}` | Once. Omitted coordinates use the world spawn; omitted `y` uses the highest block at x/z + 1. The join point must be within `max-join-distance` (default 256) of world spawn, inside the border, within world height and not inside a solid block. Rejection leaves the session authenticated and able to retry. |
| `move` | `{t, x, y, z, yaw?, pitch?}` | 20/s. Server clamps to `max-speed` (default 12 blocks/s) with 0.75 blocks of slack; invalid moves produce `self` and can close the session after repeated violations. No collision/gravity simulation. |
| `look` | `{t, yaw, pitch}` | 20/s. Rotation only. |
| `block_set` | `{t, x, y, z, state}` | 8/s combined with break. Integer coords; target must be air; reach ≤ `max-reach` (6.0) from the avatar's eye; `state` must be a placeable block. |
| `block_break` | `{t, x, y, z}` | 8/s combined. Integer coords; reach-checked; unbreakable blocks (hardness < 0) rejected. |
| `chat` | `{t, text}` | 1/s; text is trimmed to 240 chars, control characters and `§` removed. Broadcast to bridge clients and Java players as `[Web] name: text`. |
| `inv_req` | `{t}` | Returns the placeholder `inv`. |
| `held` | `{t, slot}` | `0..8`; updates the virtual held slot and returns `inv`. |
| `chunk_req` | `{t, cx, cz}` | 2/s. Requests one chunk (begin/sections/end). Allowed within `view-distance + 2` chunks of the avatar. |
| `ping` | `{t, id?}` | 2/s. `id` is echoed unchanged. App-level ping complements WebSocket pings. |
| `leave` | `{t}` | Server closes with 1000. |

### Server → client

| `t` | Schema | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `hello_ok` | `{t, protocol, id, name, tokenRequired, server:{name,version,minecraft}, limits:{maxClients,viewDistance,reach,maxSpeed,tickHz}}` | Session accepted. |
| `joined` | `{t, protocol, id, name, world, dimension, minY, maxY, tickHz, viewDistance, reach, maxSpeed, spawn:{x,y,z,yaw,pitch}}` | World joined; avatar exists. |
| `inv` | `{t, size:41, held, items:[], virtual:true, note}` | Inventory handshake placeholder. `items` is reserved for a later milestone. |
| `chunk_begin` | `{t, world, cx, cz}` | Client should clear/replace that chunk's sections. Missing sections are air. |
| `section` | `{t, cx, cz, sy, y, palette:[...], runs:[...]}` | One 16³ section, palette + RLE. See below. |
| `chunk_end` | `{t, cx, cz, sections}` | `sections` = number of section messages sent for this chunk. |
| `stream_done` | `{t}` | Initial view radius has been queued and sent. |
| `block` | `{t, world, x, y, z, state, by, source}` | Authoritative block update from a bridge (`source:"web"`) or Java (`source:"java"`) change. |
| `player_join` | `{t, player:{id,name,kind:"web",x,y,z,yaw,pitch}}` | Another bridge avatar appeared. |
| `player_leave` | `{t, id}` | Bridge avatar left. |
| `player_move` | `{t, id, x, y, z, yaw, pitch}` | Broadcast at most 10 Hz to other bridge clients. Interpolate. |
| `players` | `{t, players:[{id,name,kind:"web"\|"java",x,y,z,yaw,pitch}]}` | Full snapshot at 5 Hz, including Java players and bridge avatars in the same world. |
| `entities` | `{t, entities:[{id,type,x,y,z,yaw,pitch}]}` | Nearby non-player entities at 2 Hz, radius 48, max 128. Bridge avatars excluded. `type` is a namespaced entity type key. |
| `chat` | `{t, from:{id,name,kind}, text, ts, source}` | Java or bridge chat. |
| `pong` | `{t, id, now}` | Echo of app ping. |
| `self` | `{t, x, y, z, yaw, pitch, teleport:true}` | Server correction for a rejected move. Apply as a teleport. |
| `error` | `{t, code, message}` | Non-fatal unless followed by a close. |

### Section encoding

`section` covers a 16×16×16 block volume. `palette` is an array of block-data strings; index `0` is
always `"minecraft:air"`. `runs` is a flat array of `[runLength, paletteIndex, runLength,
paletteIndex, ...]` whose run lengths sum to exactly **4096**.

Block iteration order is local **Y outer, Z middle, X inner**:

```
index = localY * 256 + localZ * 16 + localX      // 0..4095
worldY = y + localY
worldX = cx * 16 + localX
worldZ = cz * 16 + localZ
```

`sy` is the absolute section Y coordinate (e.g. `-4` for the overworld's lowest section); `y` is
`sy * 16`. Sections that contain only air are omitted: treat a missing section as all air. A
`chunk_begin` must be followed by zero or more `section` messages and then `chunk_end`.

Example: one stone block at local index 4095, everything else air:

```json
{"t":"section","cx":0,"cz":0,"sy":4,"y":64,
 "palette":["minecraft:air","minecraft:stone"],
 "runs":[4095,0,1,1]}
```

The initial join streams chunks outward in rings within `view-distance` (default 2 → 5×5 chunks),
one chunk per two server ticks, full world height, skipping all-air sections. `chunk_req` can fill
in chunks while walking; the plugin also enqueues a new view ring when the avatar's chunk changes.

## Authority and limits

| Item | Default |
|---|---|
| Max simultaneous clients | 16 |
| `hello` timeout | 10 s after WebSocket upgrade |
| Max inbound JSON message | 32 KB (WebSocket layer rejects frames > 64 KB) |
| WebSocket heartbeat | ping every 20 s; close if silent for 75 s |
| Move / look | 20 messages/s each |
| Block intents | 8/s combined |
| Chat | 1/s, 240 chars |
| Chunk requests | 2/s |
| App ping | 2/s |
| Initial view | 2 chunks (configurable 0..8) |
| Reach | 6.0 blocks from the avatar eye |
| Speed | 12 blocks/s, +0.75 block tolerance per update |
| Join distance from world spawn | 256 blocks (0 = unlimited) |

The server validates join positions, world height, world border, reach, target block state, chunk
load state, block hardness, name uniqueness and token/origin. It does **not** simulate player
collision, gravity, fall damage, line-of-sight or inventory. A browser can fly within the speed
limit; blocks are not obstacles for the avatar. Block physics triggered by `setBlockData` (falling
sand, water flow, etc.) are not forwarded; only the explicitly changed block is broadcast.

## Errors and close codes

Common `error.code` values: `bad_json`, `bad_message`, `not_authenticated`, `already_hello`,
`auth_failed`, `protocol_mismatch`, `bad_name`, `name_in_use`, `world_not_found`, `bad_position`,
`spawn_too_far`, `outside_border`, `spawn_blocked`, `already_joined`, `not_joined`, `bad_move`,
`bad_look`, `bad_block`, `block_occupied`, `block_empty`, `unbreakable`, `out_of_reach`,
`chunk_not_loaded`, `chunk_out_of_range`, `chunk_error`, `rate_limited`, `bad_chat`, `bad_slot`,
`unknown_message`, `internal`.

WebSocket close codes: `1000` normal, `1001` going away, `1003` binary unsupported, `1009` message
too large, `1011` internal, `1012` bridge restarting, `1013` slow client, `4001` auth failed, `4002`
protocol mismatch, `4003` movement rejected, `4008` hello timeout.

## Future extension points

Protocol v2 may add a binary section frame (deflate or palette-indexed bytes), inventory/container
messages, entity metadata/skins, block-entity data, multi-world joins, and `wss`. Message types are
open-ended: unknown client messages receive `unknown_message` without closing, so additive fields and
types are safe. The inventory handshake is deliberately present but empty to reserve the flow.
